{{short description|Russian mathematical physicist}}
'''Vladimir Savel'evich Buslaev''' (Владимир Савельевич Буслаев, 19 April 1937, Leningrad<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ioffe.ru/trade_union/Photos/physfac67/professors/buslaev.html|title=professors|website=www.ioffe.ru}}</ref> – 14 March 2012) was a Russian [[mathematical physicist]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://math.nw.ru/site/en/people/Vladimir.Buslaev/|title=Staff — Buslaev Vladimir Savelievich (1937 - 2012)|website=math.nw.ru|access-date=2015-11-05|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304235124/http://math.nw.ru/site/en/people/Vladimir.Buslaev/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education==
Buslajew received his Ph.D. (Russian [[candidate of sciences|candidate degree]]) in 1963 from the [[Saint Petersburg State University|University of Leningrad]] under [[Olga Ladyzhenskaya]] with thesis ''Short-Wave Asymptotics of Diffraction Problems in Convex Domains''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=55066|title=Vladimir Savel'evich Buslaev}}</ref> He was a professor at [[University of Leningrad|Saint Petersburg State University]].

==Contributions==
He did research on mathematical problems of [[diffraction]] and the [[WKB approximation|WKB method]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.ams.org/journals/spmj/2014-25-02/S1061-0022-2014-01283-6/|title=On the mathematical work of Vladimir Savel'evich Buslaev|journal=St. Petersburg Mathematical Journal|mr=3114847|volume=25|year=2014|pages=151–174|doi=10.1090/S1061-0022-2014-01283-6|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1963 he received the prize of the [[Saint Petersburg Mathematical Society|Leningrad Mathematical Society]].

In 1983 he was an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Warsaw and gave a talk ''Regularization of many particle scattering''. He received an honorary doctorate from the [[Paris 13 University|Université Paris Nord]]. In 2000 he received the State Prize of the Russian Federation and he was an Honoured Scientist of the Russian Federation. In 2000 he gave a plenary lecture (''Adiabatic perturbations of linear periodic problems'') at the annual meeting of the [[German Mathematical Society]] in Dresden.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.tu-dresden.de/num/dmv/L206.html|title=L206|website=www.math.tu-dresden.de|access-date=2015-11-05|archive-date=2005-01-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050122085950/http://www.math.tu-dresden.de/num/dmv/L206.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He was awarded a 2000 [[State Prize of the Russian Federation]] for "Asymptotic Methods of Studying the Equations of Mathematical Physics", along with Mikhail Karasev and Arlen Ilyin. {{ill|(see list)|ru|Государственная_премия_Российской_Федерации}}
